ann_27.text: Through this part, giving a4 its first value slightly raises the predicted probability of 'yes' for the typical case, and moving a6 away from its first value or a4 from 2 to 3 slightly lowers it, all staying below 1%.
Giving a2 the value 1 or 2 instead of 3 also slightly raises it, and moving a1, a3 or a5 away from its first value slightly lowers it (on the training data only).

ann_28.text: Through this part, moving a1, a3 or a6 away from its first value clearly raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to above 99%.
For the typical case with a3 = 2, giving a2 or a4 its first value clearly lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' from above 99% to below 1%, while with a3 = 1 it stays below 1%.
For the typical case with a6 = 2, giving a2 its first value clearly lowers it from about 81% to below 1%, while with a6 = 1 it stays below 1%.

For the typical case itself, giving a2 or a4 its first value through this part slightly lowers the predicted probability of 'yes', which stays below 1%, and the a4 effect is slightly larger when a2 = 1.

ann_29.text: This part of the model acts on 305 of the 345 training cases, and 99 of them are actually 'yes'.
For the typical case it acts on (a1 = 1, a2 = 3, a3 = 1, a4 = 2, a5 = 2, a6 = 1), it slightly changes the predicted probability of 'yes', which stays below 1% (on the training data only).

Through this part, changing a6 from 1 to 2 raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to above 99% when a5 is other than 1, and to about 81% when a5 = 1 (on the training data only).
For the typical case it acts on, moving a3 away from its first value slightly lowers the predicted probability of 'yes', which stays below 1%.
Moving a5 away from its first value, or giving a1 or a4 the value 3, slightly raises it, and moving a6 away from its first value slightly lowers it (on the training data only).
For the typical case with a3 = 2, giving a4 the value 3 slightly lowers it, from above 99% to about 97%.

ann_30.text: This part of the model reads only a5 and acts on 173 of the 345 training cases, 65 of which are actually 'yes'.
For the typical case it acts on (a1 = 2, a2 = 3, a3 = 2, a4 = 2, a5 = 2, a6 = 2), it slightly changes the predicted probability of 'yes', which stays below 1% (on the training data only).
Through this part, a5 = 2 or a5 = 4 slightly lowers the predicted probability of 'yes' compared with a5 = 1 (on the training data only).

ann_31.text: This part of the model, which reads only a3, barely changes the predictions.

ann_32.text: In the model as a whole, moving a5 away from its first value slightly raises the predicted probability of 'yes' for the typical case, which stays below 1% (on the training data only).
Changing a2 from 3 to 2 slightly raises it, and changing a4 from 2 to 3 slightly lowers it, both staying below 1%.

ann_27.original: Additive per-attribute score (the linear backbone). Measured per attribute value relative to the all-low baseline, the direct edges give large positive credit when an attribute takes its first value: a6=1 +11.94, a1=1 +10.22, a2=1 +6.63, a4=1 +6.22, a3=1 +4.12, but only +2.63 for a5=1; non-first values add 0 or a penalty (a4=3 -4.60, a2=3 -3.07, a1=2 -3.00, a1=3 -1.71, a2=2 -1.91, a5=4 -0.26). Node 1948 = ReLU(0.827 - 0.090 z(a1:2)) never clips (it takes only 0.70 or 0.89), so it is an affine relay of a1:2 folded into the a1=2 penalty. The score rises roughly linearly with the number of first-values among a1, a2, a3, a4, a6 and is the rising edge of the model's response peak. Evidence: closed form is linear (sensitivities on train equal the direct weights exactly; 1948 takes only 0.70/0.89 on train, never clipping).
ann_27.proposed: An additive score: through it, first values of a2 and a4 slightly raise the predicted probability of 'yes' and moving a1, a3, a5 or a6 away from its first value slightly lowers it; a2 = 2 and a4 = 3 differ slightly from a2 = 3 and a4 = 2.

ann_28.original: At-least-three-of-five veto. Node 274 = ReLU(-1.34 + 3.46 z(a1:1) + 4.56 z(a2:1) + 4.67 z(a3:1) + 3.98 z(a4:1) + 4.48 z(a6:1)) counts first-values of a1, a2, a3, a4 and a6 (a5 is NOT included). Per-indicator increments are 7.2 to 9.7 on a base of -19.2: with two or fewer indicators the pre-activation is at most -0.2 (exactly 0 output), with three it is at least +5.6. Node 2786 = ReLU(0.605*274 - 0.609) never clips while 274 is on, so the exit id_suppress = -7.14*274 - 6.56*2786 = -11.11*274 + 4.00 whenever 274 fires, i.e. a penalty of -70 or more (-269 with all five), which forces the output to 0. ann_32.original: Two-of-five peak with an a5 handicap. The output is sigmoid(s) with s = -2.363 + Lin + Veto + 2.547*Gate - 0.599*A5 + 0.735*Inert, where Inert is identically 0. Lin (linear_first_value_score) rises by +4..+12 for each first value among a1, a2, a3, a4, a6 and is the rising edge: with at most one such first value s < 0 on all 432 configurations (max -0.42). Veto (atleast3_of_five_veto) is exactly 0 for at most two first values and <= -70 for three or more, so it is the falling edge: s < 0 for every configuration with three or more. Gate (a5_a3_bonus_gate) adds +8.5..+11 when a5 != 1 (more when a3 = 1) and nothing when a5 = 1 and a3 = 2; A5 is a -0.72 penalty for a5 in {2,4}. Inputs a4:2, a5:2, a6:2 have no enabled connections and are zero-effect entries. reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
